materiality_analysis.reason: The disclosure details CFTC registrations and, crucially, the limitations on capital transfers between broker-dealers and affiliates imposed by SEC/CFTC net capital rules. This represents a specific constraint on the company's liquidity management and capital resource flexibility, which is material financial information. Its removal obscures this operational constraint.

comparisons.peer_summary: The Corporation and its banking affiliates are subject to U.S. banking regulator capital rules, including Basel 3, and are classified as Advanced approaches institutions required to report under both Standardized and Advanced approaches, using the one yielding the lower ratio for assessment.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citi and Bank of America disclose that their derivatives and trading subsidiaries are subject to distinct regulatory capital regimes separate from their general banking holding company framework. Citi specifically notes that CGMI is subject to SEC and CFTC net capital rules that limit capital-intensive operations and capital transfers to affiliates. Similarly, Bank of America states that its banking entity affiliates are subject to capital adequacy rules issued by the OCC and Federal Reserve, and as Advanced approaches institutions, they report risk-based capital ratios under specific regulatory frameworks.

sentences.text: CGMI is also subject to SEC and CFTC rules that specify uniform minimum net capital requirements.

Compliance with these rules could limit those operations of CGMI that require the intensive use of capital and also limits the ability of broker-dealers to transfer large amounts of capital to parent companies and other affiliates.
The Federal Reserve, OCC and FDIC (collectively, U.S. banking regulators) jointly establish regulatory capital adequacy rules, including Basel 3, for U.S. banking organizations.

As Advanced approaches institutions, the Corporation and its banking entity affiliates are required to report regulatory risk-based capital ratios and risk-weighted assets under both the Standardized and Advanced approaches.

comparisons.peer_topic: GS Bank USA capital and leverage ratios
comparisons.peer_summary: The filing presents GS Bank USA's leverage ratios, defining average adjusted total assets, the Tier 1 leverage ratio, and the Supplementary Leverage Ratio (SLR). As of both December 2024 and December 2023, GS Bank USA was in compliance with applicable capital requirements for swap dealers and security-based swap dealers.
comparisons.comparison: Citi and Goldman Sachs both disclose that specific subsidiaries registered as swap dealers are subject to distinct capital requirements imposed by the CFTC and SEC. Citi states that CGMI and other subsidiaries are registered as swap dealers and subject to SEC and CFTC net capital rules. Goldman Sachs similarly notes that GS Bank USA is a registered swap dealer and security-based swap dealer and was in compliance with applicable capital requirements for these designations.

sentences.text: Citibank, CGMI, Citigroup Energy Inc., Citigroup Global Markets Europe AG (CGME) and CGML are also registered as swap dealers with the CFTC (see below).
CGMI is also subject to SEC and CFTC rules that specify uniform minimum net capital requirements.
GS Bank USA is a registered swap dealer with the CFTC and a registered security-based swap dealer with the SEC.
As of both December 2024 and December 2023, GS Bank USA was subject to and in compliance with applicable capital requirements for swap dealers and security-based swap dealers.

peer_results.rationale: While JPMorgan discloses general regulatory restrictions on cash usage and intercompany lending, it does not provide comparable details regarding specific net capital rules for futures commission merchants or swap dealers limiting capital transfers to affiliates, which is the specific focus of Citi's disclosure. The JPMorgan disclosures focus on broad reserve requirements and secured lending limits rather than subsidiary-specific net capital compliance for derivatives entities.

comparisons.peer_topic: MS&Co. Regulatory Registrations and Capital Compliance
comparisons.peer_summary: MS&Co. is registered as a broker-dealer, futures commission merchant, and swap dealer, subjecting it to SEC, CFTC, and Exchange Act capital requirements. As of December 31, 2024 and 2023, the firm exceeded all applicable net capital, tentative net capital, and notification requirements.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citi and Morgan Stanley disclose that their subsidiaries engaged in futures, swaps, and broker-dealer activities are subject to specific net capital requirements from the SEC and CFTC. Citi highlights that compliance with these rules limits capital-intensive operations and transfers to affiliates. Morgan Stanley states that MS&Co. is registered as a broker-dealer, futures commission merchant, and swap dealer, subject to SEC and CFTC capital requirements, and operates with capital in excess of these regulatory minimums.

sentences.text: In the U.S., CGMI is a member of the principal U.S. futures exchanges and clearinghouses, and Citi has subsidiaries that are registered as futures commission merchants and commodity pool operators with the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC).

Compliance with these rules could limit those operations of CGMI that require the intensive use of capital and also limits the ability of broker-dealers to transfer large amounts of capital to parent companies and other affiliates.
MS&Co. is registered as a broker-dealer and a futures commission merchant with the SEC and the CFTC, respectively, and is registered as a swap dealer with the CFTC.
At December 31, 2024 and December 31, 2023, MS&Co. exceeded its net capital requirement and had tentative net capital in excess of the minimum and notification requirements.
